transcript:
Header: 2026-04-15 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~60m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Priya (Solutions), Liam (CTO), Sofia (Head of Platform), Evan (ML Eng), Tara (Security)

Summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization for an inference POC. Discussed QPS targets, concurrency, token distributions, KV/prefix caching expectations, success criteria (latency, accuracy, cost), and a benchmark plan + timeline. Shared links: benchmark spreadsheet (goo.gl/example) and pilot SOW (drive link).

Topics: workload shape, peak vs steady QPS, token length distribution, concurrency, model variants to test, latency SLOs, security/compliance checklist, timeline for a 4-6 week pilot.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. Quick intro, I'm Maya from Redwood, with Omar our SE. We wanted to run through the workload modelling so the pilot benchmarks reflect production.
[00:18] Liam Patel: Yep, thanks. Quick context — Aurum Pay uses LLMs for transaction summarization, fraud triage suggestions, and a small conversational assistant for merchant support. All of it is sensitive so security is big.
[00:35] Omar Ruiz: Great, that helps. Can you give ballpark traffic? QPS, concurrency, and long tail token sizes?
[00:45] Sofia Gomez: Steady state is around 25 QPS across our EU+US regions. Peak spikes during morning and payroll pushes can hit 180-220 QPS for ~10 minutes. Concurrency we see typically 12-20 active requests, bursts up to 200.
[01:05] Evan Ross: Request mix: about 60% single-turn summarizations (input ~60-150 tokens, output ~20-50), 30% classification/triage (short prompts, ~40-80 tokens, small output), 10% longer conversational flows that can need up to 700 tokens in the context (we often stream).
[01:30] Maya Chen: Good detail — helps us size. For the POC we usually test both steady-state 24h run and a burst stress test. For modeling, we'll want the token distribution: short (<128): 70%, mid (128-512): 20%, long (>512): 10%. Does that line up with you?
[01:45] Evan Ross: Yes that's a fair split. A note — about 35-40% of requests include a long customer context/prefix that benefits from KV cache or prefix caching. So cache hit rate is important.
[02:05] Omar Ruiz: Noted. What's your latency SLO?
[02:08] Liam Patel: For front-end merchant flows we need P95 < 400ms ideally; P99 under 1s. For async triage/batch scoring we can tolerate 1-2s. Cost target is also important — we can't exceed X cost per 1k requests (we gave a band in the RFP).
[02:30] Maya Chen: For those SLOs — hosted Redwood API with a 13B quantized model typically hits P95 ~300-450ms depending on sequence length; Dedicated/Private with pinned GPUs drops that to ~150-300ms. We'll propose model variants to test: 13B quantized, 33B hybrid, and a 70B float for quality comparisons.
[02:55] Sofia Gomez: Sounds good. Also want to understand throughput: what's the expected QPS per GPU for those models under your runtime?
[03:05] Omar Ruiz: Approx numbers: 13B quantized can handle ~60-80 QPS per GPU for short requests (<=128 tokens) with batching. 33B hybrid around 18-25 QPS, 70B float around 6-10 QPS. Those are rough and depend on batch sizes and latency windows. We'll validate with benchmarks.
[03:30] Evan Ross: Important — we have a strict a11y and audit requirement: all calls must be logged (audit trail), and customer data must be encrypted in transit and at rest. We use AWS KMS; does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[03:50] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated support KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. We'll include our security whitepaper and SOC2 doc.
[04:05] Tara Lim: Also SSO and RBAC — we'll need SAML and role-based access for the console/API keys.
[04:12] Priya Nair: We support SAML SSO and fine-grained API key roles; we'll share the SSO integration doc.
[04:20] Liam Patel: Fine. Benchmark plan?
[04:23] Omar Ruiz: Plan outline: 1) dry-run with 1000 synthetic requests to confirm harness, 2) 24-72h steady-state run at 25 QPS shape with sampled token distribution, 3) burst tests with ramp to 200 QPS for 10-15 minute windows, 4) latency percentiles and cost-per-1k analysis, 5) quality checks on a sample of outputs against your labels. We'll run the same harness across the three model variants so we can compare latency vs cost vs quality.
[04:50] Evan Ross: For quality we'll supply ~500 labeled examples for summarization and classification so we can compute automated metrics (ROUGE / accuracy) plus a small human review.
[04:58] Maya Chen: Great. Acceptance criteria suggestions from our side: P95 <= 400ms for the chosen model variant in Dedicated or acceptable tradeoff in hosted; accuracy delta from baseline model <= 2-3% for critical flows; cost target within the band you provided. We can tune batching and quantization to meet cost/latency tradeoffs.
[05:22] Sofia Gomez: One question about caching: how does the KV cache behave across instances in Dedicated? We want cache to persist per-customer to reduce recomputation on repeated merchant contexts.
[05:34] Omar Ruiz: Our runtime supports prefix and KV caching; in Dedicated we can configure sticky routing and customer-scoped caches. For Private (VPC) you can also pin cache volumes to the cluster. We'll document the cache TTLs and eviction policies. There may be minor variation in cross-node cache hits depending on routing.
[05:55] Liam Patel: Any recommended concurrency/batching knobs for our bursty profile?
[06:00] Omar Ruiz: For bursts we recommend adaptive batching with a latency cap — e.g., target 50-80ms batch window for short requests to maintain sub-400ms P95. Also configure autoscale burst buffers so Dedicated can spin up extra workers during short spikes. We'll provide example config.
[06:20] Evan Ross: From a measurement perspective we need per-token cost breakdown and token counts in the report, plus a per-request trace to see fallbacks and model switches.
[06:30] Maya Chen: We'll include token-level cost and route-level traces in the benchmark outputs. The console has per-route breakdowns; we'll hand over exports.
[06:40] Priya Nair: Quick note on data residency: you said EU+US regions. For production we can deploy regionally; for the POC we can run EU region first if you prefer.
[06:50] Sofia Gomez: Start EU to satisfy some merchant residency restrictions, then add US.
[06:55] Maya Chen: Timeline proposal: kickoff and infra creds week of 2026-04-27 (1 week), harness setup & initial dry run 1 week (2026-05-04), full benchmarks 2 weeks (2026-05-11 to 2026-05-25), analysis and decision 1 week (2026-05-26 to 2026-06-01). Overall ~5 weeks. Does that match your timeline?
[07:15] Liam Patel: Yes 4-6 weeks looks right — we're targeting a decision before our next board meeting in early June.
[07:25] Tara Lim: Security pre-reqs: we need SOC2 report, encryption details, data retention policy, and incident response SLA.
[07:34] Maya Chen: We'll attach SOC2 and the security packet.
[07:38] Omar Ruiz: For the benchmarks, couple of technical notes we discussed: - we'll run both quantized and float models; - we'll instrument KV hit rate; - we'll capture P50/P95/P99 latency and per-token throughput; - we'll run trace samples to inspect reasons for any tail latency (GC, NVLink, network).
[07:58] Evan Ross: Also please include cost normalization sheet — cost per 1k short requests, 1k mixed requests, and cost per 1k long requests so we can map to our billing model.
[08:10] Maya Chen: Absolutely — that's in the benchmark spreadsheet template.
[08:15] Sofia Gomez: Any blockers for infra? We need to know required IAM roles and network ports so our infra team can prep.
[08:22] Omar Ruiz: We'll send an infra checklist: minimal egress for the harness, S3/GCS access for logs, and if Dedicated/Private we'll need cross-account role or provisioning details.
[08:33] Liam Patel: Cool. One last thing — fallback behavior. If the Dedicated pool is saturated, can we fall back to hosted variants? We want graceful degradation.
[08:42] Maya Chen: Yes, smart routing and fallbacks are supported. You can set policy to failover to a lower-cost model or to a hosted pool with different SLAs. We'll include sample policies.
[08:55] Evan Ross: Ok that's good.
[09:00] Maya Chen: Recap of next steps: I'll send SOW/pricing and security docs; Omar will share benchmark pack and harness; Evan will provide sample requests; Tara will confirm security checklist. Then we schedule kickoff week of 4/27.
[09:18] Liam Patel: Good meeting, thanks.

Notes / Artifacts referenced: benchmark spreadsheet (goo.gl/example), pilot SOW (drive link), security packet (drive link).

End.
